handfixes.summary: XERO_TENANT_ID is sourced into the per-request Headers map (Xero-Tenant-Id header on every call)
handfixes.why: Xero requires the Xero-Tenant-Id header on EVERY call alongside the bearer token. The env-var wiring (XERO_TENANT_ID -> Headers) is hand-wired in config.go and pinned by config_auth_test.go; a reprint drops it and every call 401/403s.

handfixes.why: Xero's per-resource ID field names (BankTransactionID, ContactID, InvoiceID, JournalID, PaymentID) are hand-wired for ExtractResourceID; the generator only templated accounts/items. handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For xero the manifest gained: XERO_AUTHORIZATION_URL, XERO_BASE_URL, XERO_CLIENT_ID, XERO_CLIENT_SECRET, XERO_TENANT_ID, XERO_TOKEN_URL. server.json gained: XERO_AUTHORIZATION_URL, XERO_BASE_URL, XERO_CLIENT_ID, XERO_CLIENT_SECRET, XERO_OAUTH2, XERO_TENANT_ID, XERO_TOKEN_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: XERO_AUTHORIZATION_URL, XERO_BASE_URL, XERO_CLIENT_ID, XERO_CLIENT_SECRET, XERO_TENANT_ID, XERO_TOKEN_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: XERO_NO_CONFIG_WRITE makes every credential write a no-op (token cache included) while leaving the `auth logout` erase working, and the MCP server honours it too (issue #270)
handfixes.why: Issue #270, raised by @Xenith-B off the back of #266. #266 stopped env-supplied client credentials reaching disk; the MINTED access token still landed in ~/.config/<tool>-cli/config.toml in cleartext and there was no supported way to turn that off. Their workaround was `--config NUL`, which is OS-specific, undocumented, makes doctor report a false 'not configured', and - the part that matters most - does not cover the MCP servers at all, because internal/mcp resolved its own hardcoded config path and ignored --config. Three deliberate boundaries make this switch honest rather than merely quiet. (1) ClearTokens keeps calling save() directly: it is the ERASE path, and routing it through the guard would make `auth logout` silently inert, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed. (2) `auth login`, the only command on this connector that writes a credential on purpose (its `auth --help` lists login, logout, setup, status), REFUSES and names the variable rather than reporting a save that did not happen - a false success is the same defect class as a doctor that says credentials are fine without checking. (3) newMCPClient now resolves through config.Load(""), the resolver the CLI uses, so the MCP server honours both XERO_CONFIG and this switch; that is the half the issue says is uncovered today. The variable is declared on all three install channels because for a Claude Desktop install the manifest prompt is the ONLY channel that can set an environment variable. Class C, new documented surface. GENERATOR-class: a reprint drops the switch entirely and silently restores the plaintext token cache.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit <PREFIX>_NO_CONFIG_WRITE (or an equivalent) as part of the standard config surface, with the same three boundaries: the erase path exempt, explicit save commands failing loudly rather than no-oping, and the MCP server resolving its config through config.Load("") instead of a hardcoded home-relative path. The hardcoded path in internal/mcp/tools.go is a generator defect in its own right - it makes --config and <PREFIX>_CONFIG inert for every MCP install on every connector.

asserts.contains: | `auth login` | Refuses, naming the variable, instead of reporting a save that did not happen. |

handfixes.summary: local analytics open the store read-only, count only AUTHORISED cash, never add across currencies, read payables as credits, take a payment's contact from its document, and date journals
handfixes.why: Codex 2026-11-02 rounds 1-2 on the novels, each against a shape Xero's OpenAPI documents: an MCP read created the store; DELETED payments and DELETED/VOIDED bank transactions counted as cash; USD and EUR summed into one total; CREDITORS (NetAmount negative) reported a -200 variance on a tied bill; payments carry no top-level Contact; journals carry only CreatedDateUTC. The novels are copied from the PUBLISHED tree on a reprint, so these pins stop an older copy coming back.

handfixes.summary: an unconfirmed MCP call writes no local state: MCP child processes never journal or derive learnings, and sync --dry-run walks a throwaway store
handfixes.why: Codex 2026-11-02 round 2 (unconfirmed-local-write): every MCP read-only tool ran the companion CLI's Execute, whose deferred journalInvocation appended to the learn journal, and the confirm gate's --dry-run preview of sync created the SQLite store. The MCP server marks its children with XERO_MCP_CHILD, so journalInvocation and deriveFlagCorrections return for them (a spoofed marker only turns journaling off). Both sites are in generated files (root.go, sync.go); a reprint drops them silently.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand: internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one credkit.Declarations literal, both mains start with credkit.Start(credwire.Declarations) and end with credkit.Exit, every HTTP client (API, OAuth token exchange and refresh, --deliver webhook and Spacefast, feedback, probe) goes through credkit.Transport, every SQLite handle through the credkit.SQLDriver internal/credsql registers, every program file write through the kit, child processes (browser open, shellout) through credkit.StartCommand and RunCommand, and the MCP stdio and HTTP servers through credkit.MCPTools, MCPIn, MCPOut and MCPHTTP (outermost: a write-free preflight, then the kit around the gate that answers the Origin, bearer and body-limit verdicts). The config, the credential store, the legacy config a save scrubs and the Spacefast delivery record are sources, written outside the kit (cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile).
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the connector's own layer. It retires secret-echo-decoded-funnel (replaced by the shared credential kit; the 4.35.1 reprint had already dropped its files, and it is not a `retired` record because check_handfixes.py accepts only registry-backed retirements and fleet_handfixes.json marks that id delegated). Classes closed, each by a test seen failing first on the pre-kit build 6515d00b3f: an API error that echoes part of the bearer (TestAPIErrorEchoOfBearerIsWithheld, CLI, --agent and MCP); a token-endpoint error that echoes part of the client secret and refresh token (TestTokenEndpointEchoOfClientSecretIsWithheld); the bearer refused to another origin and over plain http, and the refresh grant refused to a token URL on another origin (TestHeldCredentialRefusedOffOriginAndOverPlainHTTP); a credential in a malformed config or credentials file held before startup output, from the default path, XERO_CONFIG and --config (TestStartupOutputNeverShowsMalformedFileCredential); a profiles.json value under a credential flag held at startup, legacy store included (TestProfileCredentialValueHeldAtStartup; xero has no --base-url flag, so a profile base-url is never applied); the learn journal, written with credkit.AppendFile, never records a held credential (TestJournalNeverRecordsAHeldCredential), which closes the journal class; a --stdin body held before anything prints, --dry-run preview included (TestStdinBodyCredentialHeldBeforeAnythingPrints); and SPACEFAST_TOKEN held (TestSpacefastTokenHeld). `feedback --stdin` keeps its body: compactStdinBody takes a command line that starts with feedback off stdin before the kit reads it and RestoreFeedbackStdin hands it back after Start (TestFeedbackStdinIsRecorded). The OAuth token URL is configurable (XERO_TOKEN_URL, token_url) but Origins are static, so the client secret, refresh token, auth code and PKCE verifier may go to https://identity.xero.com and to the base_url origin only (the quickbooks shape; the class harness serves its token endpoint on the base URL origin); a token URL on any other origin is refused, fail closed. The auth code and PKCE verifier are held as minted:auth-code and minted:pkce-verifier, not as a `code` field, which would hold every Xero account Code. In-process tests never run Start, so cliutil.OutboundGuard, Hold and HoldBody are variables the test mains swap (root_test.go, credkit_seam_test.go). The MCP sql value cap moved from sqlite.Limit on a held connection to the _length_limit DSN parameter, and the read-only opener runs select 1 because the kit's connection does not forward Ping.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring, the Declarations literal and one kit-wrapped SQLite driver name, and let Origins follow a configured token URL the way BaseURL follows the base URL.
